question: Will foreign companies stay in Ukraine?

lines.text: Steel giant ArcelorMittal says it can no longer safely run its Kryvyi Rih plant in Ukraine.
The reason: four missile strikes on the plant in five weeks.
Reuters reports the strikes were Russian. The latest hit on 21 September.
Five people were killed and seventeen injured, one of them critically.
About 17,000 people work there, Interfax-Ukraine reports.
It is Ukraine's largest producer of rolled steel.
Since February 2022, the company says it has put in more than 700 million dollars to keep it running.
Now it expects a one billion dollar impairment charge.
Chief executive Mauro Longobardo says they are "no longer able to safely operate" the plant.

scene.quote: no longer able to safely operate

lines.text: The company says it will now focus on preserving the infrastructure.
Kryvyi Rih is also President Zelensky's home town.
JP Morgan analysts say Ukrainian supply disruptions could tighten Europe's steel supply and support prices.
One of the world's biggest steelmakers has stopped a Ukrainian plant. Will other foreign companies stay?
